title: Random-forest digital pathology quantifies P2RY12 differences in lung carcinoma subtypes
summary: The November22 v2 of a preprint first posted June17 describes a QuPath random forest trained on manually annotated tumor, stromal and immune cells for tumor-specific P2RY12 quantification. In a cohort containing319 lung adenocarcinomas and157 squamous-cell carcinomas, P2RY12 was higher in squamous carcinomas and discriminated subtype (AUC0.916); digital measurements were concordant with microscopic scoring. Classifier training used project-wide annotations and ROC validation was internal; the reviewed v2 does not establish a significant overall-survival association, independent-cohort validity or treatment benefit.

evidence.tested: Random-forest tissue classification supported tumor-cell staining quantification. Manual scoring and digital measurements were compared; subtype ROC/cutoff assessment used internal bootstrap and repeated cross-validation, with no independent cohort.
evidence.unknown: Classifier training used annotations from the project, while bootstrap/cross-validation assessed the biomarker cutoff internally; no independent cohort is established. The reviewed v2 reports nonsignificant survival association. The cached v1/v2 API abstracts both state nonsignificance, so no claim is made that v1 significance was reversed.
evidence.ai_role: A trained QuPath random forest categorized cells as tumor, stroma or immune, allowing automated quantification of tumor-cell P2RY12 staining across tissue microarrays.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv latest v2 PDF: abstract; QuPath random-forest tissue-classification Methods; retrospective cohort, ROC/statistical Methods and survival Results. Primary API v1/v2 version metadata/abstracts were compared; v1 full Methods not reviewed.
